angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 584,388 km at 63.10 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.8468 +/- 0.0213 mas (same row, RUWE 0.91): 63.10 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.84 +/- 0.12 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-65 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract): 584,388 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.87 +/- 0.1 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-65 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5213 +/- 336 K from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-65 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-65 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-65.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.529, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
